 Live .  14,585 viewing 14585 viewing England take two early wickets against Pakistan in tri-series opener
 Tue 20 Oct 2026 , Men's One Day International Series Pakistan (batting) vs England, in play Pakistan Pakistan In Play England England 47 -2 ( 10.2 ) Yet to bat Pakistan are 47 for 2 with 39.4 overs remaining Pakistan innings: 47 for 2 from 10.2 overs, in play
 England: yet to bat Live Reporting (active) 
 Scorecard 
 Summary
 Atkinson strikes with first ball of match ; Baker bounces out Saim 
 Quiz: Name line-up from England's last ODI tri-series match in 2015 
 England win toss and field first
 Match in Rawalpindi part of tri-series also including Sri Lanka
 Listen: Stephen Fleming on ambitions and vision for England 
 Close form Have your say on England men this winter
 Get involved Live Reporting
 by Timothy Abraham
 get involved Get Involved published at 09:48 BST 09:48 BST 
 Use the form on this page 
 Saim Ayub is probably the most consistent opener I've ever seen - at getting out early, that is!
 Starry, Bradford

 Post published at 09:48 BST 09:48 BST 
 Steven Finn 
Former England fast bowler on BBC Test Match Special 
 I'm surprised that England have not tried to bounce Babar Azam yet. We have seen him face difficulties against the short ball in the not too distant past.
 0 0 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Pak 46-2 published at 10 overs 10 overs 
 Saad Baig gets himself off the mark with deft use of soft hands as he guides Gus Atkinson through the vacant third region for four. 
 Nicely done.
 That boundary just releases a modicum of the pressure building on Pakistan.
 A couple of balls later and Saad is confident enough to crisply drive one a fraction too full and floaty from Atkinson through the covers for four.
 2 2 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Pak 34-2 published at 9 overs 9 overs 
 "Wow!" shouts Harry Brook at first slip as Will Jacks manages to fizz one past the bat of Babar Azam at the start of his second over.
 A couple of balls later and Babar nudges a single to get off strike.
 The left-handed Saad Baig is taking his time, playing patiently, and keeps out the rest of the over.
 10 4 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 How's stat?! published at 09:39 BST 09:39 BST 
 Saad Baig comes into this tri-series off the back of a decent run of form for PCB Greens in the National Champions Cup. 
 From four innings the 19-year-old managed 177 runs at better than a run-a-ball with a fifty in the final. 
 He plays for the Karachi Kings in the PSL where he has one fifty from his first 14 games.
 5 2 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Pak 33-2 published at 8 overs 8 overs 
 Fans still coming into the Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium in their dribs and drabs.
 Saad Baig gets his first look at Gus Atkinson and content to see off five dots.
 The young Pakistan wicketkeeper made 39 in his first innings in international cricket against Sri Lanka a couple of days ago.
 2 1 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 How's stat?! published at 09:37 BST 09:37 BST 
 Sonny Baker has struggled to find a consistent line and length so far this morning, and has persisted with bowling short - eventually getting the reward of Saim Ayub's wicket.
 Image source, Cricviz 
 3 4 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Pak 32-2 published at 7 overs 7 overs 
 Image source, Getty Images Solid start from Will Jacks, who finds a little bit of drift.
 Just a single to Babar Azam off the over.
 19 1 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 09:33 BST 09:33 BST 
 Steven Finn 
Former England fast bowler on BBC Test Match Special 
 England will be very grateful for those two early wickets because it looks like a good pitch. But they have been gifted wickets which puts them above in the game.
 It's a chance for England to put pressure on the young Saad Baig.
 24 4 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Pak 31-2 published at 6 overs 6 overs 
 Wicketkeeper Saad Baig, playing in his second ODI, is the new batter for Pakistan.
 Will Jacks is limbering up.
 14 0 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 09:31 BST 09:31 BST 
 Alex Hartley 
Former England bowler on Test Match Special 
 What was that shot? After a little bit of fortune for Saim Ayub the ball before he tries to pull it around the corner and follows it through to fine leg.
 It's not a great shot. Another weak dismissal.
 24 5 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 09:30 BST 09:30 BST 
 Aatif Nawaz 
Test Match Special commentator on BBC Radio 5 Sports Extra 
 England have another early wicket. Both openers are back in the dressing room for Pakistan.
 31 4 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 WICKET published at 5.5 overs 5.5 overs 
 Saim c Curran b Baker 8 (Pak 31-2) 
 Image source, Reuters It's short again from Sonny Baker and Saim Ayub takes on the hook shot.
 However, the Pakistan batter does not make clean contact and ends up sending it high into the hazy sky 
 Sam Curran has to wait and age but manages to hang on.
 A bit soft, but England are delighted.
 214 2 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Pak 31-1 published at 5.4 overs 5.4 overs 
 Image source, Getty Images Sonny Baker is tighter with his first couple of deliveries in his third over of the day before Babar Azam dabs him into the pitch down to third for a single.
 Harry Brook is stationed at mid-off offering a word or two in Baker's here.
 Baker's fourth delivery climbs off the pitch and is edged by Saim Ayub, but it's way wide of the diving Jodran Cox
 Saim played that late but Baker will feel he is in the game.
 13 1 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 How's stat?! published at 09:25 BST 09:25 BST 
 Image source, Getty Images A wayward start for Sonny Baker in his first two overs. Just one delivery of his first 12 was challenging the stumps.
 7 22 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Pak 25-1 published at 5 overs 5 overs 
 Saim Ayub has faced only a handful of deliveries. It's largely been the Babar show.
 Saim manages to work it out to deep cover where England scramble to make sure it does not cross the boundary.
 Atkinson hits Babar on the pad with his penultimate delivery, but contains his appeal. Way too high.
 2 2 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 09:22 BST 09:22 BST 
 Alex Hartley 
Former England bowler on Test Match Special 
 A little bit of a tame start for Pakistan but over the last two overs they have started to get things going. 
 Those boundaries have given them a bit of a boost.
 7 15 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Pak 22-1 published at 4 overs 4 overs 
 Image source, Getty Images Shot of the day so far from Babar Azam, who is oozing class here.
 Slightly overpitched from Sonny Baker and the Pakistan right-hander unfurls a sublime cover drive for four.
 Later in the over Baker bowls a bit straight and Babar shuffles across his crease and deftly flicks it off his hip for another.
 9 9 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 How's stat?! published at 09:19 BST 09:19 BST 
 Image source, Getty Images Today was the 74th time a wicket has fallen on the first ball of an ODI, and the fourth time this year. Previous instances this year:
 Pakistan v Australia - Lahore, 2 June
 Netherlands v Nepal - Utrecht, 29 July
 South Africa v Australia - Johannesburg, 27 September
 Today's stats will be supplied by Cricviz's Rufus Bullough 
 24 0 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Pak 12-1 published at 3 overs 3 overs 
 Not much in this pitch for the bowlers so far, by the looks.
 Gus Atkinson strays on to the pads of Babar Azam's pads and he effortlessly flicks it fine for four.
